results.summary_before: This design displays a 480x480 pixel Tiny Tapeout logo on a VGA monitor, using compressed data and dithered colors to fit into a single tile. It generates standard VGA signals including red, green, blue, horizontal sync, and vertical sync. The design requires an external VGA PMOD and a VGA monitor for operation, and it has been tested successfully by a silicon tester who confirmed the video works as expected. Notable features include the large resolution crammed into a small area and the use of dithering for color effects.

The documentation is extremely sparse, providing only a one-line description and a rhetorical question, so little is known about the specific visual or audio content. results.summary_before: This is a simple VGA tennis game where four input pins move the left and right paddles and additional inputs reset the score and select the ball speed. It outputs VGA signals through a Pmod, with a pin option selecting between mole99 and Digilent VGA pinouts. The design needs a VGA Pmod and a monitor plus buttons to play. The documentation is brief and does not describe the internal game logic in detail.
